The Narrative Tenses with Conjunctions
You can relate stories using narrative tenses with different conjunctions to better show the relationship between the events.

You can use various conjunctions with the Past Perfect to show when the events happened.
You can use: after, as soon as, before, once, and *till/until.
  • I read the newspaper after I had made breakfast. (The action of making breakfast was completed first before the action of reading the newspaper.)
  • After I had made breakfast, I read the newspaper.
  • As soon as I had gotten my VISA, I booked my trip to Italy. (I got my VISA first and then I booked my trip.)
  • Once I had booked my trip to Italy, I told my mother.
  • James wouldn't leave until/ till his children had given him a hug.

You can also use by the time + Simple Past or when + Simple Past in the time clause with Past Perfect in the main clause.
  • By the time I arrived at the party, my friends had already left. (My friends left the party before I arrived.)
  • When I called to invite my friend to dinner, she told me that she had already eaten.
After it had been released it generated 14 million dollars in relief.
Till and until are the same word. Till is less formal.

Concession Clauses
You can use concession clauses to express ideas that are contradictory to what is mentioned in the main clause.

If you want to talk about something that is surprising or unexpected, based on what is said in the main clause, you can use a concession clause.

You use certain words to signal a concession like although and even though. These are followed by a subject + verb.
  • Although the team played really well, they lost 3-1.
  • The team lost 3-1 even though they played really well.

You can also use despite and in spite of. These expressions are followed by a noun or a verb –ing form. They do not introduce a clause like although and even though, but the meaning is similar.
  • Although she had a starring role in the movie, she didn't earn as much money as her co-stars.
  • Despite having a starring role in the movie, she didn't earn as much money as her co-stars.
  • In spite of her starring role in the movie, she didn't earn as much money as her co-stars.
  • She didn't earn as much money as her co-stars despite having a starring role in the movie.
  • She didn't earn as much money as her co-stars in spite of her starring role in the movie.

images.text:
What is the connection between humanitarianism and the arts? Well a lot of artists are humanitarians but the two do not always go hand in hand.
When we think of artists we often think of political unrest, activism and subversion. Art has connected us to our own human nature be it ugly or beautiful. Although many artists might be self-absorbed on a personal level, what they create can provoke social action and connection. Art has the power to heal on many levels.

The benefit concert that set the precedent for social action and change was the concert for Bangladesh in 1971. After the Bhola Cyclone in 1970, thousands of people were left destitute. Musicians such as Bob Dylan and the Beatles performed at Madison Square Gardens in New York and raised 250,000 dollars to help those who were suffering. Before the concert happened,few people in North America knew about Bangladesh, let alone the cyclone that had ravaged it.

Even if you weren't born before 1984 you have probably heard of the Live Aid song "Do They Know it's Christmas?”. Bob Geldof spearheaded the campaign and many performers from the U.K. and the U.S. collaborated on the song. The purpose of the recording was to raise money for the famine in Ethiopia. After it had been released it generated 14 million dollars in relief. Though the song was recorded quite a while ago, it is often still played around Christmas time in North America.
Another benefit recording for social action was “Sun City” in 1985. It was a protest song that was recorded in defiance of apartheid. Although it only got to #38 on the charts in America, it made over a million for anti-apartheid projects.
Until the world becomes more peaceful, and everyone has shelter, food, dignity and compassion, there will be the need of these artists and humanitarians to help to improve conditions.
